headline: Saturday is a dry, foggy-then-cloudy break before rain returns Sunday and a windy, wetter low pressure system moves in Monday, bringing gusts in the 30s and 40s mph and another round of coastal flooding risk around Puget Sound.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday is dry under weak high pressure, but fog and low clouds cover much of the lowlands, including the Puget Sound area, Saturday morning, clearing around noon before high and mid-level clouds move in for a mostly cloudy afternoon. Highs reach near 50. Saturday night stays dry with increasing high clouds.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A low pressure system off the coast brings mostly light rain Sunday, then wetter, windier weather Monday as the storm moves inland. From Sunday through Monday, expect another 1 to 2 inches of rain on the coast and up to an inch in the interior lowlands, including around the Strait and Puget Sound; snow stays at high elevations in the Cascades (above about 4,000 feet), with rain in the Olympics. Typical gusts Monday are in the 30s and 40s mph, with the strongest gusts reaching the 50s along the coast and in the northwest interior. More rain will keep the Skokomish River high with a chance of renewed flooding Sunday night and Monday, and rain and wind ease Monday night as the storm weakens and moves north into British Columbia.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday brings a break in the weather under weak high pressure. A weak, falling-apart system brings a chance of rain Wednesday and Thursday. Low pressure passes to the south late in the week, keeping western Washington mainly dry Friday, with temperatures close to average throughout.

coast: A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect from 6 to 11 AM Saturday for minor flooding at high tide along Puget Sound and the northern inland waters, including Seattle, Everett, eastern Kitsap County, the Pierce and south King County lowlands, western Skagit and Whatcom counties and the San Juan Islands. A Coastal Flood Watch covers the San Juan Islands for Sunday morning's high tide, with minor to moderate flooding possible, and lower pressure, stronger winds and rain bring another coastal flooding threat around Monday's high tide; high astronomical tides keep the threat going Tuesday. On the water, east winds develop Saturday afternoon and continue Sunday, with locally advisory-level gusts possible Sunday at the western entrance to the Strait of Juan de Fuca and on the southern coastal waters. South winds peak Monday, with a 75 to 95 percent chance of gale-force gusts on the coastal waters, 40 to 70 percent on the interior waters, and a 20 to 40 percent chance of storm-force gusts offshore; seas of 5 to 8 feet Saturday and Sunday build to 15 to 18 feet Monday, and winds stay elevated at times through the week.
watch_for: Track and strength of Monday's storm, which decides how strong the winds get
Coastal flooding at high tides Sunday (San Juans) and Monday around Puget Sound
Renewed Skokomish River flooding Sunday night and Monday
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a dry Saturday and in Monday's wind and rain arriving, but the exact track and strength of Monday's storm remain uncertain, and the Wednesday–Thursday rain chances depend on a weak, disorganized system.
